content.user_title: Secure Payment Systems for PCI DSS
content.value_statement: Payment systems can expand PCI scope when cardholder data is handled without clear controls. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code design safer payment flows with PCI DSS practices.
actual_capabilities: Explains the 12 core PCI DSS requirement areas.
Lists payment data that should never be stored.
Shows tokenization patterns for payment processor flows.
Provides encryption examples for data at rest and in transit.
Covers access control, audit logging, and input validation practices.
Compares common SAQ paths for different payment architectures.
limitations: Does not replace a Qualified Security Assessor or official PCI DSS documentation.
Does not inspect live infrastructure or validate deployed controls by itself.
Uses general examples that must be adapted to each payment processor.
Does not guarantee compliance without evidence collection and formal review.

use_cases.title: Reduce Checkout Scope
use_cases.description: Review a checkout design and move card entry to hosted pages or tokenized browser flows.

use_cases.title: Harden Payment Storage
use_cases.description: Design storage rules for tokens, encrypted PAN, audit logs, and restricted access paths.

use_cases.title: Prepare Assessment Evidence
use_cases.description: Map payment controls to PCI requirement areas before a self-assessment or external review.

prompt_templates.title: Review PCI Scope
prompt_templates.prompt: Review our checkout flow for PCI scope. Identify cardholder data touches, prohibited storage risks, and safer tokenization options.

prompt_templates.title: Design Tokenized Payments
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a tokenized payment flow for our application. Include client handling, server responsibilities, stored identifiers, and audit evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Build Control Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a PCI DSS control checklist for our payment system. Cover encryption, access control, logging, vulnerability management, and policy evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Remediation
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these PCI gaps and create a remediation plan. Prioritize data exposure, compensating controls, owners, evidence, and assessment readiness.

output_examples.input: Review a checkout flow that posts card details to the application server.
output: Risk: The server enters PCI scope when it receives PAN.
Recommendation: Use a hosted payment page or browser tokenization.
Evidence to collect: Processor attestation and checkout architecture diagram.

output_examples.input: Create controls for storing payment method tokens.
output: Store processor tokens and customer identifiers only.
Restrict access by role and log every read operation.
Document retention, deletion, and incident response procedures.

output_examples.input: Plan remediation after finding unencrypted PAN in a database.
output: Immediate action: stop new storage and protect existing records.
Remediation: encrypt PAN, reduce retention, and validate logs.
Assessment evidence: migration records, key management proof, and test results.

best_practices: Use hosted payment flows or tokenization before building custom storage.
Keep cardholder data out of logs, analytics, queues, and support tools.
Map each control to evidence before a PCI review begins.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill as a substitute for a formal QSA assessment.
Do not copy examples into production without processor and key-management changes.
Do not store CVV, track data, or PIN data for any reason.

faq.question: Can this skill make my business PCI compliant?
faq.answer: No. It helps plan controls, but compliance requires implementation evidence and the correct assessment process.

faq.question: Does it support PCI DSS 4.0 planning?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance maps to core PCI DSS control areas used in modern assessments.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Should my server receive raw card numbers?
faq.answer: Avoid it when possible. Hosted payment pages and tokenization usually reduce scope and operational risk.

faq.question: Does it include production-ready code?
faq.answer: No. Examples are educational and require secure adaptation, testing, and review before production use.

faq.question: What evidence should teams collect?
faq.answer: Collect architecture diagrams, access logs, encryption records, vulnerability scans, policies, and processor compliance documentation.
